results.content:
# Tempus AI's $1.5B Personalis Deal Reshapes Cancer Monitoring  
Tempus AI is buying Personalis for $1.5B to own NeXT Personal MRD testing. Inside the deal math, the $20B market, and the fight with Natera's Signatera.  
[AI Healthcare](https://ai2.work/category/ai-healthcare)  
# Tempus AI's $1.5B Personalis Deal Reshapes Cancer Monitoring  
- 1Tempus is paying $16.25 per share for Personalis, an enterprise value of roughly $1.5 billion net of the 12.5% stake it already owned, in a mostly-stock deal that sent both stocks lower on announcement day.
- 2The prize is NeXT Personal, a whole-genome tumor-informed MRD assay with a validated detection threshold near 1.67 parts per million, backed by four separate Medicare coverage decisions won between late 2025 and May 2026.
- 3Scale is the gap: Personalis ran 10,384 clinical tests in Q2 2026 while Natera processed roughly 283,000 clinical MRD units in the same quarter, meaning Tempus is buying technology leadership, not market share.
- 4Consolidation is the trend, not the exception. Natera bought Foresight for up to $450M in December 2025 and Roche agreed to buy Saga Diagnostics for up to $595M in April 2026, all inside eight months.  
For nearly three years, Tempus AI sold someone else's cancer test. On Monday, July 20, 2026, it decided to buy the company instead.
The AI diagnostics firm agreed to acquire Personalis for $16.25 per share, an enterprise value of roughly $1.5 billion net of the roughly 12.5% stake Tempus already held. The consideration is structured as a 100% stock transaction with the option to fund up to half in cash, using a floating exchange ratio capped at 0.3356 Tempus shares per Personalis share. Closing is expected in late 2026 or early 2027, pending Personalis shareholder approval and regulatory clearance.  
Investors did not celebrate. Tempus fell roughly 8% on the announcement and Personalis dropped about 13%, a reaction that says more about dilution math than about strategic logic. Because the strategy here is straightforward: Tempus wants to own the entire arc of a cancer patient's data, from the first biopsy through every recurrence scan that follows. Molecular residual disease testing is the missing piece, and Personalis built arguably the most sensitive assay in the category.
## The MRD Land Grab: Who Owns What  
MRD has become the most contested segment in diagnostics, and 2026 has been a consolidation year. Natera acquired Foresight Diagnostics in December 2025 for up to $450 million ($275 million upfront plus as much as $175 million in milestones). Roche agreed in April 2026 to fold Saga Diagnostics into Foundation Medicine for up to $595 million. Tempus buying Personalis is the third and largest move in that sequence.  
The scale asymmetry is the part worth staring at. Personalis delivered 10,384 clinical tests in Q2 2026, a 199% year-over-year jump and 33% sequential growth. Natera processed roughly 283,000 clinical MRD units in the same quarter at an average selling price near $1,275. Tempus is not buying market share here. It is buying a technically superior assay and betting its own commercial machine can close a gap measured in orders of magnitude.  
| Player | MRD Assay | Technical Approach | Scale / Status | Recent M&A Move |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Natera | Signatera / Latitude | Tumor-informed ctDNA, broadest payer coverage | \~283,000 clinical MRD units in Q2 2026, +56% YoY | Acquired Foresight Diagnostics, up to $450M (Dec 2025) |
| Tempus AI + Personalis | NeXT Personal | Whole-genome tumor-informed, \~1,800 variants, sub-10 ppm sensitivity | 10,384 Personalis clinical tests in Q2 2026; four Medicare coverage decisions | $1.5B acquisition announced July 2026, closing late 2026 / early 2027 |

results.content:
**Chicago-based Tempus AI is buying molecular residual disease (MRD) specialist Personalis, folding one of oncology’s most closely watched liquid biopsy technologies into its AI-driven precision medicine platform.**  
[Tempus AI](https://www.tempus.com/), Inc. (NASDAQ: TEM) announced on July 20, 2026, that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire [Personalis, Inc](https://www.personalis.com/). (NASDAQ: PSNL), a Fremont, California-based cancer genomics company known for its NeXT Personal MRD test. The deal ranks among the more significant consolidations in the fast-growing MRD space this year, and it deepens a partnership between the two companies that dates back to late 2023.
## Deal Terms  
Under the agreement, Personalis shareholders will receive $16.25 per share, a 6% premium to Personalis’ closing price on Friday, July 17, and a 28% premium over the company’s unaffected 30-day volume-weighted average price. The transaction carries a total enterprise value of roughly $1.7 billion, though the figure comes to about $1.5 billion once Tempus’ existing stake in Personalis, around 12.5%, is netted out.  
The consideration is structured primarily as stock. Personalis shareholders will receive a floating exchange ratio of Tempus common shares for each Personalis share they hold, capped at a maximum ratio of 0.3356 and finalized closer to closing based on Tempus’ recent trading price. Tempus can elect to pay up to 50% of the consideration in cash, which it says would be funded through cash on hand and borrowings under its existing credit facilities. The agreement also gives Personalis the right to walk away if Tempus’ Class A shares fall below $46.00 before closing, a floor that guards against too much erosion in the value of the stock Personalis holders would receive.  
Both companies’ boards have approved the transaction, which still requires Personalis shareholder approval and customary regulatory clearances. Merck, which holds roughly 13% of Personalis’ voting power, has agreed to vote its shares in favor. The deal is expected to close in late 2026 or early 2027.
## Part of a Broader Consolidation Wave  
The Tempus-Personalis tie-up is not happening in isolation. The MRD and broader liquid biopsy diagnostics space has seen a string of deals over the past year as larger platforms move to consolidate testing capabilities. In December 2025, Natera acquired Foresight Diagnostics in an all-stock transaction worth up to $450 million, $275 million upfront plus as much as $175 million in milestone payments, adding phased variant technology aimed at strengthening its MRD offerings across solid tumors and lymphoma.  
In April 2026, Roche agreed to acquire Saga Diagnostics for up to $595 million, folding the company’s structural-variant MRD platform into its Foundation Medicine subsidiary; leadership there described MRD testing as one of the fastest-growing segments in diagnostics. That transaction is expected to close by the third quarter of 2026.  
Tempus itself has been acquisitive in adjacent areas. In August 2025, it acquired Paige, an AI-enabled digital pathology platform, for $81.25 million, adding a large library of digitized pathology slides, clinical reports, and genomic data, infrastructure that could plausibly work in tandem with Personalis’ MRD assets going forward.
